outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $18,500. Notes: This range is the time to approval if the Conditional Use Authorization and building permit are granted. It covers the CUA (120–300 days from filing to Commission approval per the 2007 outdoor dining case at 1650 Haight St and typical CUA timelines) and the building permit (14–120 days). The CUA is the critical path: pre-application meetings and preparation add 4–8 weeks before filing, environmental review and neighborhood notification add 60–90 days, and hearing scheduling takes another 30–60 days. If Planning determines at the pre-application meeting that the outdoor area is principally permitted under PC § 202.2(a)(7), the timeline drops to 14–120 days for the building permit and health permit only (submitted in parallel), and the cost drops to $800–$15,000 building permit plus $1,298–$3,500 health plan check and permit, totaling roughly $2,100–$18,500. The cost range shown assumes a CUA is required: approximately $3,100–$15,000 for a CUA (depending on construction valuation and fee waiver eligibility, based on catalog entry for sf.conditional_use_authorization) plus $800–$15,000 building permit, excluding the health permit fees already included in other approvals. These figures are government fees only and exclude architect, expediter, and construction costs. The outdoor dining cases at 1650 Haight St took 128 days (CUA filed Sept 2007, approved Jan 2008) plus 12 days for the variance, and at 1640 Haight St took 36 days (agency referral filed April 2013, approved May 2013), showing the wide range depending on the permit path.
